quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results from the call: 'fourth quarter revenue of $1.53 billion, non-GAAP gross margin of 38.2%, and earnings per share of $0.64, both exceeding the midpoint of our guidance.' Power Solutions Group (PSG) revenue was $724 million, 'a decrease of 2% quarter over quarter and a decrease of 11% year over year'; automotive revenue was $798 million (up approximately 1% QoQ) and industrial $442 million (up approximately 4% QoQ and up 6% over 2024, the first year-over-year growth after eight quarters of declines). Manufacturing utilization fell to 68% as planned, and Q4 gross margin carried approximately 700 basis points of underutilization charges. Full-year 2025 free cash flow was a record $1.4 billion (24% of revenue, up 17% year over year), approximately 100% of it returned through buybacks, and a new $6 billion repurchase program was announced in November.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.53 billion revenue; non-GAAP gross margin 38.2%; EPS $0.64; PSG $724 million; 2025 free cash flow $1.4 billion (24%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 guidance: 'We anticipate Q1 revenue will be in the range of $1.44 billion to $1.54 billion in line with normal seasonality at the midpoint' - the first quarter with expected year-over-year growth since the downturn started over three years ago. Non-GAAP gross margin between 37.5% and 39.5% (up 30 basis points at the midpoint in a quarter where margins have historically declined, credited to FabRite cost actions), non-GAAP EPS $0.56 to $0.66, capex $35 to $45 million, utilization rising to the low 70% range. The guide absorbs $50 million of non-core revenue exits in Q1 (about $40 million in Q4); excluding them revenue would be above seasonal. The CFO said Q2 exits 'are probably gonna be somewhere around $100 million' and the CEO put the full-year exits at about 300 ('it's a 300 total'); the business is being exited on margin and pricing pressure and is neutral to gross margin. Q2 normal seasonality is up 3% to 4%, and utilization is expected around the mid-seventies for Q2 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $1.44 billion to $1.54 billion; non-GAAP gross margin between 37.5% and 39.5%; EPS $0.56 to $0.66; $50 million non-core exits in Q1

quarterly_data.signal: AI data center sizing at the start of 2026: 'We delivered more than $250 million in AI data center revenue across the PowerTree' in 2025, a business the CEO said came 'from almost nothing' and whose growth rate 'accelerated from '24 to '25 and will continue.' No 2026 guide for the segment (it is reported inside the 'other' category), but the CFO said 'We do expect that our AI data center revenue in Q1 will grow high teens percentage-wise' and the CEO said the year is starting with better growth than last year. Asked whether AI data center could become a double-digit share of revenue as some peers target, the CEO answered 'it's a matter of the when, not the if.' Part of the 2025 AI data center revenue was driven by the SiC JFET.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $250 million AI data center revenue (2025); Q1 AI data center revenue to grow high teens

quarterly_data.signal: Design wins across the AI data center PowerTree: onsemi is sampling its 1,200-volt ultra-low RDS SiC JFET for AI data center platforms as more platforms move to higher-voltage bus architectures (power supplies, battery backup disconnect, hot swaps). At the UPS stage it won a high-end design with 'a leading US power supply supplier' (not named) that cuts the system footprint by about 50% using onsemi's SiC power module, with production volumes starting this quarter. At the rack level: 'we have secured designs for our SiC and silicon MOSFET and our SiC JFET in both the BBU and PSU systems with Delta, Lite-On, and Great Wall to serve both their Western and China customers'. At the XPU board level it secured several next-gen design wins with multi-phase controllers, smart power stages and point-of-load devices, and began sampling dual five-by-five VCORE solutions and two-phase power modules on a TLVR (transinductor voltage regulator) architecture, building on the VCORE assets acquired in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,200-volt SiC JFET sampling; UPS design win cuts footprint by about 50%

quarterly_data.signal: High-voltage positioning for the AI rack: the CEO said onsemi is 'the only company or one of the very few companies that are able to do the high voltage, think 800 volts with our 1,200 volt devices all the way to the SPS type devices closer to the core', that new architectures are 'collapsing the conversion tree' so a supplier needs both high- and low-voltage parts, and that onsemi is 'targeting where the market is going to be in a few years which is the high voltage rail'. Near the XPU it serves standard GPUs as well as non-standard GPUs and ASICs. Asked why the updated investor deck shows a much larger per-rack content opportunity for 2030 than for 2027, the CEO attributed the increase to 'more products mapping onto more content that we can address with our portfolio' (SiC JFET, vertical GaN, five-by-five and SPS point-of-load). The per-rack dollar figures were quoted by the analyst, not by management.

GaN roadmap: 'This year, we are preparing to sample more than 30 new GaN devices spanning 40 to 1,200 volts, including both discrete devices and integrated driver plus GaN solutions', from low-voltage parts near the XPU to 1,200-volt parts for automotive and industrial. Lateral GaN uses a foundry model: 'We have an engagement or a partnership with Innoscience and a partnership with GlobalFoundry. So we'll be doing the switches or the switching element with those partners', combined with onsemi's Treo control and driver silicon into a smart switch sold as an onsemi product, with revenue beginning in 2026. Vertical GaN (VGaN) is proprietary GaN-on-GaN technology made in onsemi's US fab, a native single 1,200-volt device rather than stacked lateral parts, aimed at AI data centers, EVs, renewables and aerospace/defense; onsemi is collaborating with GM on electric drive systems and expects first VGaN revenue in 2027. Treo products sampling doubled year over year and the new design funnel is now over $1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 30 new GaN devices; 40 to 1,200 volts; first VGaN revenue in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Gross-margin bridge toward the 53% long-term target (CFO): about 700 basis points from lifting utilization from the 70% range to the low nineties, another 200 basis points of FabRite actions, roughly 200 basis points from the $160 million of fixed cost from the earlier fab divestitures once that manufacturing comes inside, and 200 basis points plus from new products at favorable margins. FabRite cut fab capacity by 12% in 2025, and additional footprint measures were announced in Q4; 'These actions together will lower our 2026 depreciation by approximately $45 to $50 million', with the gross margin impact in the second half. Utilization flows into gross margin with a lag of about two quarters; reaching low-90s utilization would take roughly 25% higher revenue at today's mix. The CFO said a gross margin with 'something with a four handle is within sight, assuming that the market continues to recover.'
quarterly_data.figure: 700 basis points underutilization; 200 basis points FabRite; $160 million fixed cost; 53% gross margin target; fab capacity reduced 12%

quarterly_data.signal: Demand visibility improved versus 90 days earlier (CEO): 'Book to bill is trending up. We are walking into the quarter with less turns needed than the prior quarter. Expedites, we're seeing more expedites than we did ninety days ago', though onsemi is 'not seeing the replenishment yet.' Automotive inventory digestion is 'largely behind us' and industrial has bottomed; tier-one auto suppliers are not restocking because of thin margins, which the CEO said sets automotive up for 'a risky ramp when the demand does pick up.' Q1 by end market: auto roughly flat, industrial down low teens, other up low single digits. Balance-sheet inventory was 192 days, including 76 days of strategic inventory being depleted over the next two years (base 117 days), and distribution inventory rose to 10.8 weeks, within the 9 to 11 week target.
quarterly_data.figure: distribution inventory 10.8 weeks; 192 days inventory (76 days strategic)

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon carbide and energy storage: in EVs onsemi keeps 'a major share in China, which is all silicon carbide' because those platforms are on 800 volt, is still gaining share in North America and proliferating with European OEMs; design-ins are done and the work is now proliferation. onsemi will not convert its SiC furnaces to 300 millimeter: 'you're not gonna see a CapEx cycle going to the furnaces or substrate manufacturing.' Outside the data center it leads the utility string energy storage (ESS) market with more than 50% worldwide share, is ramping its IGBT hybrid power module to multiple global customers, and its next-generation SiC MOSFET hybrid power module (efficiency nearing 99.5%, 430 kilowatts power density) has a first win at SunGro in their global platform.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 50% worldwide share (utility string ESS); efficiency nearing 99.5%; 430 kilowatts
